subject: SLA maintenance & uptime redlines — escalation paths and credit formulas
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena.park@novacloud.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: Samir Hossain <samir@novacloud.com>, Priya Singh <psingh@saleslaw.co>
Date: 2026-08-17T20:22:00Z
Subject: SLA — requested clarifications on uptime definition & maintenance

Hi Jonas,

Thanks for sending the draft SLA. Our legal and SRE teams reviewed and pushed back on a few items — summarized below so you and your ops/legal folks can propose final language: 

1) Uptime target: We prefer 99.95% monthly uptime for Production endpoints. 99.9% materially increases our risk profile.
2) Measurement window: uptime should be measured per monthly calendar window and exclude scheduled maintenance (see below) and force majeure. Please include a clear formula for how downtime is calculated (total downtime in minutes / total minutes in month).
3) Service credits: request sliding scale credits starting at 5% for <99.95% to 50% for <99.0%, with monthly cap at 50% of fees.
4) Incident response: P1 acknowledgement within 30 minutes, P1 remediation SLA 4 hours (business hours), P2 acknowledgment 2 hours, remediation 24 hours.
5) Maintenance windows: prefer weekly maintenance window of Sun 02:00–04:00 PT (with 72h advance notice) and no more than 4 hours/month of planned downtime counted against SLA.
6) Escalation path: include phone-based P1 escalation to on-call SRE and VP of Ops contact details.

I've attached a redlined Word doc with the specific clause language our counsel prefers (NovaCloud_Requested_Changes.docx). Please review and let us know where you can compromise. 

Best,
Elena
Elena Park
Sr. Cloud Ops Program Manager — NovaCloud Solutions

--
Attachment: NovaCloud_Requested_Changes.docx (docx, 62KB)

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@novacloud.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-17T21:10:00Z
Subject: Re: SLA — requested clarifications on uptime definition & maintenance

Elena — thanks for the clear summary and for the redlines. Quick reaction and a counterproposal from our side: 

- Uptime target: We can agree to 99.95% for Production if we limit the definition of covered endpoints to "Customer production inference endpoints" (i.e., excludes sandbox and internal tooling). For hosted shared models we need compatibility language; request a short carveout for experimental models.
- Measurement: we agree on monthly calendar window. We'll supply the exact formula in the contract: (Total Minutes in Month - Minutes of Unavailable Service) / Total Minutes in Month * 100. Scheduled maintenance and emergency maintenance with notification won't count toward unavailability.
- Service credits: propose the following sliding scale (monthly fees): 99.95–100.00% = 0 credits; 99.5–99.95% = 5% credit; 99.0–99.49% = 15% credit; <99.0% = 30% credit. Cap at 30% of monthly fees. This cap is important for us operationally.
- Response times: We can commit to P1 acknowledgement within 30 minutes and P1 target remediation (best-effort) within 4 hours; hard remediation guarantees are tough across varied customer workloads, so propose "target remediation" language plus an operational review if repeated misses occur. P2: acknowledgement 2 hours, target remediation 24 hours.
- Maintenance windows: Accept weekly maintenance window of Sun 02:00–04:00 PT (we'll define in UTC in final doc) and owner will provide 72 hours notice for planned maintenance. Limit planned maintenance to <=4 hours/month counted as maintenance (additional planned maintenance to be scheduled with Customer support).
- Escalation: we'll add on-call phone + pager escalation; add Redwood VP of Ops as secondary.

I've attached a marked-up PDF highlighting concrete clause wording: Redwood_SLA_markedup_20260817.pdf. Next steps: Laura (legal) and Marissa (customer success) — can you convert our counter- language into redline-ready contract text? Rishi, please confirm ops can meet the on-call acknowledgement/phone escalation.

Thanks,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Head of Sales — Redwood Inference 

--
Attachment: Redwood_SLA_markedup_20260817.pdf (pdf, 48KB)

From: Priya Singh <psingh@saleslaw.co>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, Elena Park <elena.park@novacloud.com>
Cc: Samir Hossain <samir@novacloud.com>
Date: 2026-08-18T09:30:00Z
Subject: Re: SLA — requested clarifications on uptime definition & maintenance

Jonas / Elena — Priya here (external counsel supporting NovaCloud). A couple of precise redlines from our side to consider adding into the SLA language to avoid ambiguity: 

- "Downtime" definition: explicitly exclude (i) scheduled maintenance where Customer was given >=72 hours notice, (ii) force majeure events, (iii) Customer-caused outages (misconfiguration, API keys revoked), and (iv) third-party infra outages not under Redwood control.
- Measurement: require Redwood to provide a downloadable uptime report with raw minute-level data and incident tickets for the month on which a credit claim is based.
- Credits: NovaCloud prefers a 50% monthly cap. If Redwood cannot accept 50%, please consider allowing a right to terminate for material repeated failures (e.g., >2 months in 6 months below 99.0%).
- Emergency maintenance: require prior notice "wherever reasonably possible" and a post-incident RCA for any emergency maintenance that impacted Production.

We can circulate a short set of redlines for insertion into the MSA and Order Form if that helps. 

Regards,
Priya Singh
Partner, SalesLaw Co.

From: laura_bennett@redwood.com <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@novacloud.com>, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-18T12:05:00Z
Subject: Re: SLA — proposed language and compromise on credits

Hi all,

Thanks — I reviewed the asks and Priya's notes. Suggested compromise we think is reasonable and easier to sign quickly: 

1) Uptime: Redwood accepts 99.95% for Customer production endpoints (as Jonas indicated). We'll add explicit exclusions: scheduled maintenance with >=72 hours notice, emergency maintenance, Customer-caused issues, and force majeure.
2) Credits: counterproposal: sliding scale with cap at 30% monthly fees (as Jonas proposed) but include an additional commercial remedy: if Customer experiences >=2 months in any rolling 6-month period below 99.0%, Customer may pursue termination for cause with 30 days' cure period. This addresses NovaCloud's termination concern while keeping our credit exposure bounded.
3) Measurement & audit: Redwood will provide monthly uptime reports plus incident ticket exports supporting credit claims. If Customer disputes, both parties will meet to review the raw data; we can add a 3rd-party measurement clause only in extreme disputes.
4) Response/acknowledgement: we'll commit to P1 acknowledgement within 30 minutes (phone + ticket) and target remediation 4 hours (operational target, not a fee trigger). P2: ack 2 hours, target remediation 24 hours. If multiple misses occur (>3 P1 misses in a quarter), we'll add an SLA improvement plan and executive review.
5) Maintenance: planned maintenance will be limited to 4 hours/month (counted against maintenance bucket). We'll provide 72 hours notice for planned maintenance; emergency maintenance will be communicated ASAP with a post-incident report.

If this is acceptable, we can incorporate the language into the MSA/Order Form and circulate a DocuSign envelope. Elena/Priya — please let us know if the termination-for-cause compromise for repeated poor performance is acceptable in lieu of a higher credit cap.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: Redwood_SLA_Counter_Redlines.docx (docx, 29KB)

From: jonas_weber@redwood.com <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Elena Park <elena.park@novacloud.com>, Priya Singh <psingh@saleslaw.co>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-18T16:22:00Z
Subject: Re: SLA — proposed language and compromise on credits

Elena / Priya — appreciate the quick turnaround and the constructive compromise. Laura's compromise looks good from Sales/legal and Rishi confirmed ops can meet the acknowledgement targets and provide the monthly reports we described.

Let's proceed: Laura, please fold the agreed language into the MSA and Order Form redlines. Marissa, please prepare the DocuSign envelope and include the marked-up PDF and the NovaCloud requested changes doc as attachments.

Elena — once you confirm the termination-for-cause compromise (two months below 99.0% in any rolling six-month window with 30-day cure), we'll send the DocuSign link.

Jonas
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
